text.tspan: Amazon FSx: fully managed third-party high-performance file systems
• SMB 2.0-3.1.1, native Windows (NTFS), ACLs, user quotas
• Linux EC2 can mount it too (cifs-utils)
• DFS Namespaces: group many file systems
• Up to 12 GB/s, 350,000 IOPS, 64 TB per FS;
• On-prem access over VPN / Direct Connect
• Automatic daily backups to S3 (7 days default)
• ML, HPC, video, financial modelling, EDA
• TB/s throughput, millions of IOPS, sub-ms
• Link S3 buckets: read S3 as files, write results
• NFS, SMB, iSCSI (+ NVMe/TCP): high OS compatibility
• Move ONTAP or NAS workloads to AWS
• Linux, Windows, macOS, VMware Cloud on AWS,
• SSD tier + capacity pool that grows/shrinks
• Managed OpenZFS, NFS v3, v4.0, v4.1, v4.2 only
• Same clients as ONTAP (Linux, Windows, macOS ...)
• Course: up to 1,000,000 IOPS, < 0.5 ms latency
Docs now: up to 2M IOPS (cached), 21 GB/s,
